chunks: From him, from his father, from Safwan, from Mu'alla Abu Uthman, from Mu'lla ibn Khunays, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who travels and rides in the sea. He said, 'My father (peace be upon him) used to say, 'It harms your religion. That is how people obtain their sustenance and livelihood.'

key_terms.يَرْكَبُ الْبَحْرَ: rides in the sea / travels by sea

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man traveling by sea according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys that his father, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), viewed sea travel as potentially detrimental to one's religion because it is the primary means by which people secure their livelihood (*rizq*). This implies that the commercial nature of maritime journeys may distract from spiritual focus or involve permissible but spiritually neutral activities that compete with worship. The narration highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual implications of daily economic activities and the balance between sustenance and faith.
